translations.text: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, writes to the twelve tribes scattered abroad: Greetings!
Count it a great joy, my brothers, when you encounter our various trials.
You know that the testing of your faith produces endurance.
But let endurance complete its work, so that you may be perfect and complete, lacking nothing.
But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives generously to everyone without reproaching them, and he will give it to him.
But let him ask with faith, without doubting at all, for anyone who doubts is like a wave of the sea that the wind strikes and tosses about.
For that person must not think that he will receive anything from the Lord.
A person with a divided mind is unstable in all his ways.
But let the brother in a humble position boast in his exaltation,
and the rich man in his humiliation, because he will pass away like a flower of the grass.
For the sun rose with its scorching heat and dried up the grass. Its flower fell, and the beauty of its appearance perished. In the same way, the rich man will wither in his pursuits.
Blessed is the person who endures a trial, because, once he has proved worthy, he will receive the crown of life that he promised to those who love him.
Let no one say when he is tempted, “I am being tempted by God.” For God does not tempt anyone to evil; he himself tempts no one.
But each person is tempted by his own desire, being dragged away and deceived.
Then desire, when it has conceived, gives birth to sin, and sin, when it has reached completion, gives birth to death.
Do not be led astray, my beloved brothers.
Every good gift and every perfect gift is from heaven, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no shadow or change or turning.
By his own will, he gave birth to us through the word of truth, so that we might be the firstfruits of his creatures.
You know this, my beloved brothers. But let everyone be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to become angry.
For human anger does not produce God's righteousness.
Therefore, having put aside all filth and all wickedness, receive with gentleness the word of truth, which has the power to save your souls.
But be people who do what the word says, and not merely listeners who deceive yourselves.
For if someone listens to the word but does not do what it says, he is like a person looking in a mirror at the face he was born with.
For he looked at himself, went away, and immediately forgot what he was like.
But the person who looks closely into the perfect law of freedom and remains in it, not listening and then forgetting but doing the work, will be blessed in what he does.
Anyone who says of himself, “I am a worshiper,” but does not restrain his tongue and instead deceives his own heart—this person's worship is empty.
Worship that is holy and undefiled before God the Father is this: to care for orphans and widows in their distress and to keep oneself from being defiled by the world.
My brothers and sisters, do not hold your faith in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ while showing favoritism.
For if someone comes into your assembly with gold rings on his fingers and wearing splendid clothes, and a poor person also comes in wearing dirty clothes,
and you pay attention to the one wearing splendid clothes and say to him, “Sit here in this good place,” while you say to the poor person, “Stand,” or, “Sit here on my footstool,”
So you have made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts.
Listen, my beloved brothers and sisters: has not God chosen the poor of the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom he promised to those who love him?
But you have dishonored the poor. Is it not the rich who oppress you? Is it not they who drag you into courts?
Are they not the ones who slander the good name that was pronounced over you?
If you fulfill the law of freedom according to the Scriptures, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,” then you are doing well.
But if you show favoritism, you are committing a sin, and the law convicts you as transgressors.
For whoever keeps the whole law but falls in one matter has become guilty of all of it.
For the one who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not murder.” So if you do not commit adultery but do murder, you have become a transgressor of the law.
Speak and act as people who will be judged by the law of freedom.
For judgment is without mercy for anyone who has not shown mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgment.
What good is it, my brothers and sisters, if someone says, “I have faith,” but has no deeds? Can faith save him without deeds?
For if a brother or sister is naked and lacks food from day to day,
and one of you says to them, “Go in peace; be warm and eat your fill,” but does not give them what their bodies need, what good is it?
It is the same with faith: if it has no deeds, it is dead by itself.
But someone will say to you, “You have faith, and I have deeds.” Show me your faith without deeds, and I will show you my faith through my deeds.
You believe that God is one. You do well. The demons also believe, and they tremble.
But do you want to understand, you foolish person, that faith without deeds is useless?
Was not Abraham our father justified by deeds when he offered up his son Isaac on the altar?
You see that faith was working together with deeds, and through deeds his faith was brought to completion.
And the Scripture was fulfilled that says, “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness,” and he was called God’s friend.
You see that a person will be made righteous through deeds, and not through faith alone.
Likewise, was not Rahab the prostitute justified by deeds when she welcomed the messengers and sent them out by another road?
For just as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without deeds is dead by itself.
Not many of you should become teachers, my brothers and sisters, knowing that we will all receive a stricter judgment.
For we all stumble many times. If someone does not stumble in what he says, he is a perfect person, able to bridle his whole body as well.
Look, we put bits into horses’ mouths so that they obey us, and we turn their whole bodies as well.
Look also at the ships: although they are so large and are driven by strong winds, they are steered by small rudders in whatever direction the pilot wants.
The tongue is like this too: it is a small part of the body, yet it makes big claims. Look, a small fire burns a great forest.
The tongue too is a fire. The tongue is a world of wrongdoing among our body parts. It defiles the whole body and sets the wheel of life on fire, and it is itself set on fire by hell.
For every kind of wild animal, bird, reptile, and fish is tamed and has been tamed by humankind.
But no human being can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.
With it we bless God the Father, and with it we curse people who were made in God’s likeness.
Blessing and cursing come out of the same mouth. My brothers, these things should not happen this way.
Do springs pour out fresh water and bitter water from the same opening?
My brothers, can a fig tree produce olives, or a grapevine produce figs? Nor can salt produce fresh water.
Who among you is wise and understanding? Let him show his deeds through his good conduct, with gentleness and wisdom.
But if you have bitter envy and rivalry in your hearts, do not boast and lie against the truth.
This is not the wisdom that comes down from heaven. Rather, it is earthly, unspiritual, and demonic.
For where there is envy and rivalry, there is disorder and every evil deed.
But the wisdom from heaven is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, eager for what is good, full of mercy and good fruit. It does not discriminate or act hypocritically.
The fruit of righteousness is produced in peace for those who make peace.
Where do the wars and fights among you come from? Do they not come from your pleasures, which wage war within your body parts?
You desire and do not have. You murder and envy, yet you cannot obtain what you want. You fight and wage war. You do not have because you do not ask.
You ask and do not receive because you ask wrongly, so that you may spend it on your pleasures. You adulterers!
Do you not know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? Whoever wants to be a friend of the world will therefore become an enemy of God.
Or do you think that Scripture speaks in vain? It longs jealously for the spirit that has dwelt within us.
But it gives great grace. That is why it says, “God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.”
Humble yourselves, then, before God. Stand against the devil, and he will flee from you.
Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded people.
Be distressed, mourn, and weep. Let your laughter turn into mourning and your joy into gloom.
Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will lift you up.

My brothers, do not speak against one another. Whoever speaks against his brother or judges his brother speaks against the law and judges the law. If you judge the law, then you are not someone who obeys the law, but a judge.
There is one lawgiver and judge, who has the power to save and to destroy. But who are you to judge your neighbor?
Now then, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we will go into this city, spend a year there, do business, and make a profit”—
You do not know what will happen to you tomorrow. For your life is like a mist that appears for a little while and then disappears.
Instead, you should say, “If the Lord wills and we live, we will do this or that.”
But now you boast in your arrogance. All boasting of this kind is evil.
For anyone who knows how to do what is good but does not do it, this is sin.
Now then, you rich people, weep and cry out over the miseries that are coming upon you.
Your wealth has rotted, and your clothes have become moth-eaten.
Your gold and silver have corroded, and their corrosion will testify against you. The corrosion will eat your flesh like fire. You have stored up wealth in the last days.
Look! The wages of the workers who harvested your fields, which you fraudulently withheld from them, are crying out. The cries of those who harvested have reached the ears of the Lord of hosts.
You have lived in luxury on the earth and indulged yourselves. You have fattened your hearts for the day of slaughter.
You have condemned and killed the righteous person. He does not resist you.
Be patient, then, my brothers, until the coming of our Lord. Look! The farmer waits expectantly for the precious fruit of the earth, being patient over it until he receives it early and late.
You too must be patient and strengthen your hearts, because the coming of our Lord has drawn near.
Do not grumble against one another, my brothers, so that you will not be judged. Look! The judge is standing at the door.
My brothers, take as an example of suffering and patience the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.
Look! You call those who endured blessed. You have heard of Job’s endurance, and you have seen the outcome brought about by the Lord, for the Lord is compassionate and merciful.
Above all, my brothers, do not swear by anything—not by heaven, nor by earth, nor by any other oath. Let your yes be yes and your no be no, so that you will not be judged.
Whoever among you is suffering should pray. Whoever is cheerful should sing praises.
Whoever among you is sick should call for the elders of the church, and they should pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord.
And prayer and faith will save the sick person, and the Lord will raise him up. Even if he has committed sins, they will be forgiven him.
Therefore confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, so that you may be forgiven. The prayer of a righteous person is very powerful and effective.
Elijah was a human being like us, and he prayed earnestly that the sky would not give rain. It did not rain on the earth for three years and six months.
Afterward he prayed again, and the sky gave its rain, and the earth produced its fruit.
My brothers, if someone among you strays from the truth and someone turns him back—
But whoever turns a sinner back from his misguided path will save a soul from death and cover a multitude of sins.
